title: The World of Metals and Non-metals

concepts.learning_objective: Identify metals by their metallic lustre and hardness, and recognise exceptions such as sodium, potassium and mercury.
Define malleability and give examples of metals beaten into thin sheets.
Distinguish brittle materials from malleable ones using the hammering activity.
Define ductility and relate it to the everyday uses of metal wires.
Explain sonority as the ability of metals to produce a ringing sound.
Explain that metals are good conductors of heat and relate this to cooking vessels and their handles.
Classify materials as good or poor conductors of electricity using a tester circuit.

topics.title: Effect of air and water on iron: rusting

concepts.learning_objective: Infer from Activity 4.5 that both air and water are needed for iron to rust.
Describe corrosion of metals and the methods used to prevent rusting.

topics.title: Effect of air and water on other metals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the burning of magnesium and the basic nature of metal oxides.
Explain why a very reactive metal such as sodium is stored in kerosene.

topics.title: Substances that behave differently from metals: non-metals

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the burning of sulfur and the acidic nature of non-metal oxides.
List the properties of non-metals and use them to classify an unknown element.
Recognise that metals and non-metals are elements and that materials like plastic and wood are not.

topics.title: Uses of non-metals and metals in everyday life

concepts.learning_objective: State everyday uses of non-metals such as oxygen, carbon, nitrogen, chlorine and iodine.
Describe alloys and the special uses of metals in technology and industry.
